decision.stageInvocationMechanism: Prefect Deployment invocation through run_deployment(..., as_subflow=True), called from a Root-owned Prefect dispatch Task.
decision.deploymentModel: Each Stage specialization is registered as a distinct Prefect Deployment and executed by Process Workers.
decision.workerCapacityModel: Two independent Process Worker instances in one Process work pool, each with flow-run limit 1. The exact expected ONLINE worker set and distinct per-Stage worker assignment are enforced by the qualification script.
decision.codeSource: Prefect LocalStorage bound to the PoC source directory. The Process Workers run on the same host and can access that local path.
decision.stageResultTransport: Stage Flow persist_result=True. The Root waits for the Deployment Flow Run to reach a terminal state and loads the persisted Stage domain result through the Prefect result reference.

hierarchy.responsibility: Owns the Pipeline invocation and submits Root dispatch Tasks for the Stage Deployments.
Creates the deployment Flow Run and awaits its terminal state/result. It is an invocation mechanism, not a GPWCF Stage component.

hierarchy.prefectConstruct: Native Prefect Flow Run from a named Deployment
hierarchy.responsibility: Executes the Stage specialization on a Process Worker; retains Stage domain identity, invocation identity, input and typed domain result.

hierarchy.prefectConstruct: Native Prefect Task invoking a native Step Subflow
hierarchy.responsibility: Preserves the public Step callable boundary and native child Flow Run.
Owns SPU invocation and StepExecutionResult assembly.
Executes inside the owning Step Flow Run and returns SPUExecutionResult.

rootToStage.nativeEdge: Stage Flow Run.parent_task_run_id points to the Prefect-generated synthetic Task Run, not directly to the user-defined Root dispatch Task Run.
rootToStage.proof: The synthetic Task Run task_inputs.__parents__ contains the Root dispatch Task Run ID; the Stage Flow Run parent_task_run_id equals the synthetic Task Run ID.
rootToStage.interpretation: The relationship is preserved through a native intermediate Task. It is an indirect parent/child chain, not a direct Root Flow Run to Stage Flow Run parent edge.

stageToStep.nativeEdge: Step Flow Run.parent_task_run_id points to the Prefect-generated child-subflow Task Run.
stageToStep.proof: The synthetic Task Run task_inputs.__parents__ contains the Step dispatch Task Run ID.

stepToSpu.proof: Each SPU Task Run flow_run_id identifies its owning Step Flow Run; two SPU Task Runs are recorded for each Step invocation.

concurrency.qualifiedProfile: Two distinct Process Worker instances, same Process work pool, flow-run limit 1 each.
concurrency.repeatedEvidence: Five of five Root invocations showed positive overlap between the two sibling Stage Flow Run execution intervals.
concurrency.singleWorkerExploration: A single Process Worker configured with --limit 2 did not produce deterministic sibling Stage overlap in the exploratory trial; that profile is not accepted as the qualified concurrency configuration.
concurrency.capacityBoundary: The result qualifies two concurrent sibling Stage Deployments only. Higher sibling Stage counts and worker autoscaling/capacity are not qualified.

sameHostConstraints: The deployment pull step uses Prefect LocalStorage referencing a local source directory.
The default local result storage path is under the shared PREFECT_HOME on the same Windows host.
All qualified workers run on the same host and use the same CPython 3.15.1 environment.
Multi-host workers require shared/retrievable code storage and shared result storage; this has not been qualified.
The SQLite API server uses one API-server worker. This is separate from the two Process Worker instances.

resultSemantics.domainResult: Persisted Stage return value containing Stage identity, invocation identity, Root correlation and StepExecutionResult values.
resultSemantics.identityRule: GPWCF domain identities remain distinct from Prefect Deployment IDs, Flow Run IDs and Task Run IDs.

HI-01_rootSiblingStageFlowConcurrency.evidence: Five of five deployment-backed Root invocations showed sibling Stage Flow overlap and distinct Process Worker assignment.

HI-02_stageToStepHierarchy.evidence: Step Subflow Flow Runs and synthetic parent links were validated for twenty Step invocations. Their sibling overlap was not measured in this phase.

HI-03_stepToSpuFunctionalHierarchy.evidence: Forty SPU Task Runs were correlated to their owning Step Flow Runs; production SPU binding remains out of scope.

nonConclusions: The two-worker same-host Process profile is not a multi-host execution qualification.
The two-worker profile does not establish capacity or autoscaling for more than two concurrent sibling Stages.
The PoC does not select a shared code or result storage backend for distributed workers.
The PoC does not bind production GPWCF or Generator stage contracts.

postQualificationRuntimeState.apiListener: port 4210 no longer listening; TIME_WAIT connections only
postQualificationRuntimeState.prefectHomeAndResultStorage: preserved outside the repository at C:\poc\GPWCF\prefect-home-deployment
postQualificationRuntimeState.workPoolAndDeploymentRecords: preserved in the external Prefect SQLite database for later inspection after the local server is restarted
